page.layout: Two engraved medallion portraits at the top, side by side, each with its legend around the rim. Below them one block of running text in two paragraphs, with two small raised insertions in the second paragraph. No notes in the margins, no footnotes.

main_text.l: CAR. IX. FRANC. REX.
ISABEL. CAROLI IX.
GAL. REG. VX.
CAROLVS nonus Francorũ Rex successit Francisco se-
cũdo fratri, anno Domini,1560. Et qui ætatis suæ, vndecim an-
norũ numerũ non excedebat, Regina mater regni gubernaculis
præfuit cũ Antonio Borbonio Rege Nauarræ, maiestatis Regiæ
summũ Locũ tenente: id quod omnibus Francię ordinibus, qui
tunc Aurelię conuenerant, pergratũ fuit. Decimo octauo Maij,
1561. Carolus fuit sacratus, Rhemis à Cardinali Lotharingię Rhe-
morũ Archiepiscopo. Paulo post bellũ est exortũ. Plures vrbes
captę à nouæ religionis professoribus, quarũ aliquot à Rege re-
cuperatis, Rege Nauarræ in obsidione Rothomagi ad mortem
vulnerato; pugna cõmissa, victoribus catholicis: in qua Cõdęus
princeps capitur. Fit pacificationis edictũ 19. Martij, 1563. & iu-
ssis Regis & Condęi copiis, Portus Gracię, quem Angli tenebăt,
capitur. Paulò post, ortum nouum bellum & præliũ cõmissum,
inter Lutetiã & D. Dionysiũ, in quo Cõnestabilis Môtmoren-
cius ad mortẽ vulneratur. Denuò pax interuenit, quam paulò
post subsecuti sunt noui & ingentes tumultus bellorũ, quibus
sedatis, Pacificationis edicto nouo publicato, xi. Augusti. 1570.
Rex [?]Meseriis, Elisabetha Austriã Imperatoris Maximiliani filiã
vxorem ducit, & paulò post, fracto denuò pacificationis edicto,
respublica Gallica miserè afflictatur. Rex obiit 3. Iunij, 1574.
ELISABETHA Austria Imperatoris Maximiliã filia,
Carolo nono Francorũ Regi nupsit, 26. Nouembris 1570;
peperit filiam nomine Mariam Elisabetham. Fuit ea omnium
virtutis, modestię, humanitatis & prudentię exemplar: quũ omnibus
accedebat & faciei & totius corporis pulchritudinis
[?]summa præstantia.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are engraved in the image; they are transcribed as lines, abbreviations as printed. "Rex Meseriis" in the first paragraph is uncertain, the word is hard to read on the scan. In the second paragraph, several words are set as small raised insertions squeezed into the line ("filia", "peperit" with "pepe-" and "rit", "virtutis", "omnibus", "dinis summa"); these are placed in the text where they belong, "pulchritudinis" is partly obscured by the fold/crease at the line end. The fold through the lower right of the page is damage, not text. Words such as "Carolus", "Maij", "1560" are spaced as printed in the original.
